IT STARTS WITH UNDERSTANDING

Your questions.
A little more clarity.

You don’t need to have every answer before you begin.

How do I know what kind of care is needed?+

Begin with the person’s daily needs, preferences, and any advice from their treating doctor. Nursing, rehabilitation, and everyday assistance serve different purposes. Discuss the appropriate level of support before arranging care.

Can I plan care before a hospital discharge?+

Planning ahead can make the return home easier to organise. Discuss discharge recommendations, practical needs at home, service availability, and the intended start date before confirming a plan.

Can support fit around our family’s routine?+

Talk through preferred times, daily routines, and the tasks you need help with. Scheduling and the scope of support should be agreed in advance, based on available services.

What should I ask about the cost?+

Ask for a clear breakdown of the service, visit or shift length, equipment if needed, and any additional charges. Confirm the terms in writing before making a booking.

What information should I have ready?+

Your city, the type of support you’re considering, and your preferred timing are a good starting point. Keep medical records private and share them only through an agreed secure channel when required.
